name: Creating a Dictionary of Student-Scores Pairs (Case 2)
description: Assume we have a list of students and a list of their corresponding test scores. Construct a program that has two functions:\n- a function that receives these two lists and returns a dictionary that maps each student to the scores of that student, and \n- a function that receives the dictionary created by the above function and calculates the average score of each student

1.content: #Step 1: Define the function that creates the dictionary

commentList:
We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function create_dictionary that takes a list of students (referred by variable std_lst) and a list of their corresponding test scores (referred by variable test_lst) and returns a dictionary that maps each student to the scores of that student.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.

We first need to define a dictionary referred by variable res_dict for storing the scores of each student. We initialize it with an empty dictionary by setting it to a pair of braces {}.

We need need dictionary to store key-value pairs where each key represents a student and the value that is mapped to that key represents the list of the student's scores.

5.content: #Step 1.2: Update the dictionary entries as we iterate through the indexes in the given lists

commentList:
We need to get each student and corresponding test scores for that student. We can do this by iterating over the indexes in the given lists.

We need the list indexes to start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including the list length. We get this sequence by calling the range(len(std_lst)) function.
Note that the function len(std_lst) returns the number of the values in the students list. Also note that we could use len(test_lst) in the range function as both lists have equal number of values.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

To determine if the student at index i of the students list already exists as the key in the dictionary, we employ the in operator to test membership. Because the in operator implicitly scans the keys in the dictionary looking for a match.
std_lst[i] gives us the student at index i in the students list.
If the student at index i of the students list already exists as the key in the dictionary, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

When the student at index i of the students list already exists as the key in the dictionary, we call the function append(test_lst[i]) to add the test score at index i of the score list to the end of the list that holds student's test scores.
When the student at index i of the students list does not exist as the key in the dictionary, we need to add a new entry to the dictionary for the student.

The statement inside the body of this else statement is executed when the student at index i of the students list does not exist as the key in the dictionary. Otherwise, the body of this else statement is skipped.

We need to add the student at index i in the students list as a new key to the dictionary. We need to initialize the value mapped to this key with a list that has the test score at index i of the scores list.
Now that we created the dictionary, we need to return it.
The return statement, when reached, ends the function call and sends the result back to the caller.

12.content: #Step 2: Define the function that calculates the average of each student's scores

commentList:
We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function average that takes a dictionary mapping students to their scores and calculates the average score of each student. The dictionary is referred by variable new_dict.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.

14.content: #Step 2.1: Iterate through the students in the dictionary

commentList: We need to iterate over the students in the dictionary and calculate their average score. We can get the students by iterating through the keys in the dictionary using a for loop.

This for loop assigns the name std_name to each of the keys in the dictionary in turn, from left to right, and then the statement in the loop body will be executed for each character.

Note that each key in the dictionary represents a student.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

16.content: #Step 2.1.1: Iterate through the list of student's scores, add each score to the running total

commentList: We need variable total to maintain a running total, which means the sum of the student's scores. Of course, the total should be initialized with 0.
To calculate the average score of each student, we need to iterate over the list of student's scores. We do this by using a for loop that iterates through the list of student's scores.

This for loop assigns the name score to each of the values in the list of student's score in turn, from left to right, and then the statement in the loop body will be executed for each character.

Note that new_dict[std_name] returns the student's scores.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

We need to add each student's score to the running total that is stored in variable total. So, in each iteration, we add the student's score to the variable total and store the result into the variable total.

The += operator adds the value of variable score to the value of the variable total and the result is stored in the variable total. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement total = total + score.

20.content: #Step 2.1.2: Calculate and print the average of student's scores

commentList:
We calculate the average by dividing the sum of student's scores by the number of student's scores.

The function len(new_dict[std_name]) returns the number of the scores in the list that is mapped to the student.
Note that since we want to keep the fractional part of the division result, we need to use the real division by using / operator.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the student's name followed by the average of the student's scores. The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
We define list referred by variable names to hold the students names. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].
We define list referred by variable scores to hold the test scores. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].

This statement first calls the create_dictionary function and passes the names and scores lists as its arguments. Then, it calls the average function passing it the returned dictionary from the create_dictionary function.

Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned dictionary from the create_dictionary function call in a variable. We could use the dictionary returned from this function call directly in the average function.
Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared.
